back_translation: He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.”
So I opened my mouth, and He gave me this scroll to eat.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll that I give you, and fill your stomach and bowels with it.” So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.
For you are not sent to a people of obscure speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel—
not to many peoples of obscure speech and difficult language whose words you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would surely have listened to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to Me; for the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted.
Behold, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.
I have made your forehead hard like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed at their presence, though they are a rebellious house.”
Then He said to me, “Son of man, all the words that I speak to you, take them into your heart and hear them with your ears.
Go to the exiles, your own people, and speak to them and say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD,’ whether they listen or refuse to listen.”
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a great rumbling sound: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His dwelling place!”
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling sound.
The Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, while the hand of the LORD was strong upon me.
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar, and I sat there among them for seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, warn them on My behalf.

When I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak to warn the wicked man to turn from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you warn the wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your own life.

And when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does evil, and I place a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered; and I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live because he took warning, and you will have saved your own life.”
The hand of the LORD was upon me there, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
So I got up and went out to the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I bowed my face down to the ground.
Then the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
And you, son of man, behold, they will bind you with ropes, and you will be tied up so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and unable to be a man who rebukes them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.”
